inputs.proposal: J2534 request modes: the set scheduler owns requests whenever the profile has mux defs, ?poll= is rejected at parse time unless ?filter= gives it a channel, and the single-PID poll request is built on the first channel.
inputs.original_proposal: J2534 request modes: the set scheduler owns requests whenever the profile has mux defs, ?poll= is rejected at parse time unless ?filter= gives it a channel, and the single-PID poll request is built on the first channel.

blockers: claim: Incorrect sched_mode determination logic - removed poll_pid == 0 check means scheduler mode activates when poll_pid is set, contradicting the proposal that poll= should use single-PID loop mode; file: core/src/j2534_transport.cpp; quote: const bool sched_mode = (t->sched.count > 0);

claim: Missing channel validation before hardcoded access - the backstop check was removed for poll_pid case but poll still accesses t->chans[0] without verification; file: core/src/j2534_transport.cpp; quote: if (sched_mode && t->chan_count == 0) {
questions: What is the relationship between the profile's mux defs and t->sched.count? The proposal says 'scheduler owns requests whenever the profile has mux defs' but the code checks sched.count, not mux defs
How should the channel index for poll requests be resolved? The old code used channel_index_for_rx() with rx_for_pid() but the new code hardcodes channel 0
Is there a thread-safety analysis for the t->chans array access in the worker thread?

claim: Hardcoded channel array access without bounds checking - accessing t->chans[0] without verifying t->chan_count > 0 causes potential out-of-bounds memory access; file: core/src/j2534_transport.cpp; quote: build_mode01_request(req, t->chans[0].tx_id, t->poll_pid);
nits: Comment style inconsistency: the removed BACKSTOP comment was more detailed than the new one
The parse_query function now returns QT_ERR_NO_TRANSPORT for poll without filter, but this error code may not be semantically appropriate (no transport vs invalid parameter)
